label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

findings.quote: The same three circles, drawn in front of the room one by one, so the overlap arrives last.
findings.why: The figure caption, the narrator and the deck line all say the circles are drawn one at a time, so one slide is told three times.

findings.quote: in the first act it is allowed, in the second refused, in the third passed up to a person to decide
findings.why: The figure line, the narrator and the Studio quote ('Allowed, denied, or asked') all give the same three outcomes.

findings.quote: Three things collide; where they overlap is the story.
findings.why: It reads out the figure line above it, which already says three circles with the scenario in the overlap.

findings.quote: These are the night shift's work. ruv-sgit made the moving pictures for the talk
findings.why: The narrator reports what an agent made, with no 'I' and no hindsight; the same happens at stops 3, 6 and 11.

findings.quote: This is how a slide was made when it mattered.
findings.why: A catalogue sentence in the narrator's voice, with no sign of what the editor thought then or thinks now.

findings.quote: How to read the scenes: they are dramatised.
findings.why: It is an instruction on how to read, and a reader scanning on a phone reaches it before any scene has earned it.

findings.quote: At the end of a book about how the factory worked, here is the rest of what it made
findings.why: Thirteen stops of pages I cannot open from a phone between meetings, with nothing saying what my team could take from them; I would stop here.

findings.quote: If a fresh copy of me cannot rebuild it from the explainer and the data, it is not finished.
findings.why: This is the one line that answers my question about agents on a team, but it sits in a quoted aside under a figure I cannot see.

findings.quote: like deck's, still open when the hold came
findings.why: Deck is a cast member the glossary has not introduced, so the definition leans on a name the entry does not explain.

findings.quote: hour one runs from midnight to a minute before one, and the talk was due as hour nineteen ended
findings.why: It is a clock definition in the middle of an otherwise alphabetical list, and the order breaks here (and at 'mailroom' and 'player').

findings.quote: The check (the team called it the gate)
findings.why: Appendix B then says 'the gate before every release' and 'the check' in different rows, so the reader does not know if they are one thing.

findings.quote: a pin proves which tool it is, not that the tool is sound
findings.why: 'Pin' is not in the glossary, and the row is the one I most wanted to follow.

findings.quote: Public vaults, checked before every commit
findings.why: Vaults are not explained here or in the words list, and the tour says the page of vaults is left out.

findings.quote: that same evening the usage limit came before any hold did
findings.why: A real cost for a team like mine, but it is written as a clipped aside with no account of what the limit stopped.

findings.quote: The difference is the book's point.
findings.why: A strong claim worth saying as the editor ('I think'), not as a pointer to the book.

what_holds: 93-appendix-b-the-control-register.md: the setting versus expectation split is the first thing I could take to my own team; the two tables with 'what it missed' are frank and the failures stay in.
93-appendix-b-the-control-register.md: line 7, 'it held because nothing pushed on it', says in one sentence why expectations are weak.
91-the-words-used.md: short plain definitions, each pointing to a chapter, which is what I wanted from a glossary on a phone.
90-the-tour-at-length.md: the 'Never silent' line and the pairing of a figure, a narrator line and one agent line make each stop short enough to scan.
notes: As a team member with my own agent, I came for how a team runs with an agent each. Appendix B answers that; the tour does not, and the stops read as a gallery of pages. Record lines and %% notes skipped as a reader would.
